applies_why: The judge text decides a pressed-link collision by what the sentence says in its own words rather than by weighing the challenger's chain against the link's chain by footing.
quote: the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires
room: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse: reading one, the whole pressed chain must be weighed against the link's chain by support; reading two, the judge may decide by a single sentence's own wording
why: The judge acknowledges the challenger's analogy is footed yet resolves against it using Matthew 1:20's own words, which is the verse-by-verse stating-verse test K-C retires.
